parsed.restated: ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Group.IsFinitelyPresented G ∧ ∃ (F : Finset G) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 ∧ ∀ M : SoficGroups.PermutationModel G, ¬ SoficGroups.GoodOn M F ε
parsed.proof:
constructor
· rintro ⟨G, inst, hG, hS⟩
  refine ⟨G, inst, hG, ?_⟩
  by_contra h
  apply hS
  refine ⟨fun F ε h0 h1 => ?_⟩
  by_contra hn
  push_neg at hn
  exact h ⟨F, ε, h0, h1, hn⟩
· rintro ⟨G, inst, hG, F, ε, h0, h1, h⟩
  refine ⟨G, inst, hG, ?_⟩
  intro hS
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := hS.approximation F ε h0 h1
  exact h M hM
parsed.english: There is a finitely presented group G together with a finite subset F ⊆ G and some ε strictly between 0 and 1 such that no permutation model on a finite set is ε-good on F. That is, F cannot be approximated by almost-multiplicative, almost-free-acting permutations to within ε in normalized Hamming distance.
parsed.why_clearer: It unfolds the `Sofic` class into its explicit failure of the approximation property, so a reader sees the witnessing F and ε directly instead of a negated typeclass.
